Q6113.L1t: Arson is a common-law offense against property that is classified separately from most other crimes against persons and property.
Q6113.L2t: At common law, arson is the malicious burning of the dwelling of another, and the defendant here burned a house after forgetting to turn off a stove while intoxicated.
Q6113.L3t: Common-law arson requires malice, which means intent to burn or a reckless disregard of an obvious risk of fire, and a defendant who merely forgot to turn off a stove did not have that mental state.
Q6113.L4t: The defendant will be found not guilty because arson requires malice, and merely forgetting the stove is not malice.
Q6113.L2f: Common-law arson covers only the burning of buildings owned by the defendant himself, and the defendant here burned a house after forgetting to turn off a stove.
Q6113.L3f: Arson is a crime whose definition turns on the grade of the offense, so only a defendant who committed a felony can be convicted of it, and the defendant here committed no felony.
Q6113.L4f: The defendant will be found not guilty because he did not commit a felony, so the arson charge fails.

Q5047.L1t: Urinary catheters are used to drain urine from the bladder and need proper care by trained staff.
Q5047.L2t: Blood clots in the urine can block a urinary catheter and may be a sign of bleeding in the urinary tract.
Q5047.L3t: Repeated blockage by clots may signal a clinical problem such as bleeding, which care staff must report and not manage on their own by changing the catheter.
Q5047.L4t: You should report the repeated clot blockage to the medical staff.
Q5047.L2f: Blood clots in a catheter are harmless and normally clear up by themselves within a few hours.
Q5047.L3f: Repeated blockage means the catheter itself is faulty, and replacing it is the routine fix that care workers are expected to carry out themselves.
Q5047.L4f: You should take out the blocked catheter and insert a new one yourself.

Q5028.L1t: Land subdivision law deals with how a landowner divides a tract into lots and records a plan with the county.
Q5028.L2t: The investor recorded a subdivision plan that set aside a 10-acre lot for a school, and this was publicly promoted in his brochure.
Q5028.L3t: A recorded plan that reserves a lot for a public purpose and is promoted to buyers is a dedication of that land to the public, which gives the public a right to use it and does not impose a restriction on the use of other lots.
Q5028.L4t: The designation of the 10-acre tract for a school is best described as an easement for public use.
Q5028.L2f: A subdivision plan has no legal effect on land use until the county school board formally acquires the tract by condemnation.
Q5028.L3f: The investor's designation was a promise made to the lot buyers in the plan to limit how the land is used, for the benefit of the other lots in the subdivision.
Q5028.L4f: The designation of the 10-acre tract for a school is best described as a restrictive covenant.
